exercise.name: Cable Cross Over Lateral Pulldown

reference.title: Cable Cross over Lateral Pulldown
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder adduction, scapular depression and downward rotation, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the bar comes down to the chest, breathe in as it rises.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short pause, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull to the upper chest without swinging back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack

cues.text: Kneel tall on a mat midway between two high pulleys, one handle in each hand, arms long and reaching up and out toward the pulleys, palms forward.
Breathe out; draw the shoulder blades down and pull the elbows down and in toward the sides of the ribs, hands finishing beside the shoulders.
Elbows tucked to the ribs, chest up, shoulder blades down and together.
Breathe in and let the handles rise up and out along the same arc until the arms are long.
Full stretch at the top, ribs down, then pull again.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back as the handles come down
Pulling the hands in front of the chest like a fly
mistakes.fix: Drive the elbows down to the sides; the hands stay over the elbows.
Start each rep by setting the shoulders down.
Keep the hips over the knees.

kinematics.setup: Upper arm ≈152° from the trunk, reaching up and out toward the pulley
kinematics.peak: Elbow beside the ribs (≈14° forward of the frontal plane), hand 2 cm vs shoulder height
kinematics.norm: Frontal-plane arc: upper arms from up and out to beside the ribs (clinical opinion); lat activation is similar across pulldown hand positions (Signorile 2002)
From nearly straight to about 100-130 degrees (clinical opinion)
From about 150 degrees to about 30-40 degrees from the trunk (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Tall kneeling, ≈7° from vertical; pulleys 228 cm high, 190 cm apart
kinematics.peak: Unchanged (≈9°); cables clear of the body by at least 6.14 cm
kinematics.norm: Tall kneeling, trunk upright and still (clinical opinion; Lehman 2004)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s down, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s up
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Cross over Lateral Pulldown, video (movement reference)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)
Signorile, Zink & Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)
Lusk, Hale and Russell 2010, grip width and forearm orientation effects on muscle activity during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 24(7):1895-1900)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move with the trunk still and the shoulders down.
Kneel on a mat; return the handles one at a time to the stack before standing.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort at the top: start with the hands a little lower.
Knee discomfort: sit on a box between the pulleys instead.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps pull the arms down and back.
